# Approval Matrix and Limits
This matrix defines who can approve a purchase request or purchase order and sets their financial thresholds. All approval limits apply to the gross value of each individual document, including GST, freight, and packing charges. The policy applies from 2026-04-01.

## Rules
- Limits set who may approve a purchase request or purchase order, and up to what value [POL-APR-002 §1].
- Every limit applies to the gross value of one document, including GST, freight, and packing [POL-APR-002 §2.1].
- Limits apply to gross value including GST, not the basic value [POL-PUR-001 §5.1].
- Each limit applies per document, not per day or per supplier [POL-APR-002 §2.2].
- The role-based approval limits (gross including GST) are: Purchase executive (PUR-EXEC) at ₹2,50,000; Senior buyer (PUR-SR) at ₹5,00,000; Purchase manager (PUR-MGR) at ₹10,00,000; Plant head (PLANT-HEAD) at ₹50,00,000; Stores (STORES) has no approval authority [POL-APR-002 §3.1].
- An order or document within the raiser's own limit is approved automatically upon submission, and Bahi records the raiser as the approver [POL-APR-002 §3.2].
- An order or document above the raiser's limit routes to their manager, and then up the line to the first person whose limit covers it [POL-APR-002 §3.3] [POL-PUR-001 §5.2].
- Documents above ₹50,00,000 require the Managing Director's written approval outside Bahi, which the plant head's office then records [POL-APR-002 §3.4].
- Approvers on leave may delegate authority in writing to someone of the same or higher role for a stated period, but never to a lower role [POL-APR-002 §4.3].
- The plant head reviews this approval matrix every April and whenever the organisation changes [POL-APR-002 §6.1].

## Watch out
- Do not split one requirement into several orders to stay within an approval limit [POL-APR-002 §2.3].
- Orders for the same item from the same supplier raised within seven days of each other count as one single requirement [POL-APR-002 §2.3].
- Documents over ₹50,00,000 cause Bahi to display ERR-APR-0009 (no approver found) until recorded by the plant head's office [POL-APR-002 §3.4].
- You cannot approve a document you raised; Bahi will refuse the approval with ERR-APR-0003 [POL-APR-002 §4.1] [POL-PUR-001 §5.3].
- Integration and service accounts (such as role SYS-ADMIN or SVC_AGENT) have no approval authority; any document approved by them is invalid and must be cancelled or re-approved by a person [POL-APR-002 §4.2].
- For example, an order with a basic value of ₹2,38,000 and 18% GST (gross ₹2,80,840) exceeds a purchase executive's ₹2,50,000 limit and must route to the purchase manager [POL-APR-002 §5.1] [POL-APR-002 §5.2].

# General Purchasing Policy
This policy sets out how Rasoi Steel Works buys materials, components, and services. It ensures every rupee is spent with proper approval, from a qualified supplier, and against an open budget. All rules apply starting 2026-04-01 across applicable company units through Bahi ERP.

## Rules
- Buy all materials, components, and services with proper approval, from a qualified supplier, and against an open budget [POL-PUR-001 §1].
- Apply this policy to every purchase made for the Pune plant (RSW-PUN-01) and the Chakan unit (RSW-CHK-01) through Bahi ERP [POL-PUR-001 §2].
- Use the rate specified in the current rate contract [POL-PUR-001 §7.1].
- Record the manager's written reason in the remarks for any order placed at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate [POL-PUR-001 §7.2].
- Ensure every order carries its Bahi-assigned document number and reaches Released status before instructing the supplier to deliver [POL-PUR-001 §9.1].

## Watch out
- Do not use rates from older orders in the order history as binding prices; they are for reference only [POL-PUR-001 §7.1].
- Do not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Bahi is Released [POL-PUR-001 §9.2].

# Purchase Requests (PR)
A purchase request (PR) initiates the buying process in Bahi ERP. It captures key details such as the item, quantity, need-by date, warehouse, and cost centre before an order can be created. Approving a request routes it based on estimated value and covers subsequent order generation.

## Rules
- Every purchase must begin with a purchase request in Bahi, unless it qualifies as a direct order under §3.3 [POL-PUR-001 §3.1].
- From 2026-04-01, each purchase request must name the item, quantity, need-by date, warehouse, and the cost centre that carries the spend [POL-PUR-001 §3.2].
- Mandatory screen fields on PUR-PR-01 include Item code (F2), Quantity, Need-by date, and Cost centre (F2); optional or defaulted fields are Warehouse (F2; defaults to WH-PUN-STR), Estimated rate, and Remarks [MAN-PUR-72 §9.2].
- The request type (`pr_type`) is STD for standard requests [MAN-DD-72 §5.2, MAN-PUR-72 §9.2].
- Press F3 (Fetch) after entering the item code to automatically populate the unit of measure, warehouse, default cost centre, and estimated rate [MAN-PUR-72 §9.3].
- Request numbers follow the format `pr_no` PR/<year>/<five digits> (for example, PR/2026/04417) [MAN-DD-72 §5.1].
- Press F8 to save the request; Bahi assigns a request number and sets the status to DR (Draft) [MAN-PUR-72 §9.4].
- The estimated value (`est_value`) is calculated as: quantity × estimated rate × 1.18 [MAN-DD-72 §5.4, MAN-PUR-72 §9.4].
- Press F9 (Submit) to submit the request; if the estimated value is within your limit, it is approved immediately (status AP) [MAN-PUR-72 §9.5].
- If the estimated value exceeds your limit, Bahi routes the request up the management line to an approver whose limit covers it, marks the status PA (pending approval), and sends an email notification [MAN-PUR-72 §9.5].
- PR approval covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's limit covers the order's gross value [POL-PUR-001 §5.4].
- The system stores audit details including `raised_by`, `raised_on`, and `approved_by` [MAN-DD-72 §5.5].
- Standard database fields recorded for each request are `cc_cd` (Cost centre), `need_dt` (Need-by date), `whs_cd` (Warehouse), and remarks [MAN-DD-72 §5.3].

## Watch out
- The estimated rate fetched by F3 uses the rate from the last released purchase order for the item, not the current contract rate [MAN-PUR-72 §9.3].
- Estimated value calculations automatically apply an assumed 18% GST regardless of the item's actual tax rate [MAN-PUR-72 §9.4].
- The need-by date must be today or in the future; entering a past date triggers error ERR-PR-0105 [MAN-PUR-72 §9.6].

# Purchase Order Entry and Rules
The purchase order screen creates standard or direct orders for active suppliers in Bahi ERP. Standard orders require an approved purchase request, while direct orders are reserved for low-value purchases. Each order contains a single line item and must undergo a system fetch before it can be saved.

## Rules
- Standard (STD) purchase orders are raised against an approved purchase request, and direct (DIR) orders have no source request [MAN-PUR-72 §11.2].
- A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including GST, is ₹50,000 or less (effective 2026-04-01) [POL-PUR-001 §3.3].
- A direct order may not refer to a purchase request [MAN-PUR-72 §11.7].
- A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity (effective 2026-04-01) [POL-PUR-001 §3.4].
- Order numbers follow the format PO/<year>/<five digits>, such as example PO/2026/01182 [MAN-DD-72 §6.1].
- Mandatory header fields are Supplier code, Order type, Tax code, Cost centre, and Need-by date, along with Source PR for STD orders [MAN-PUR-72 §11.5].
- Mandatory line fields are Item code, Quantity, and Rate [MAN-PUR-72 §11.6].
- Header fields also include payment terms and warehouse; remarks are optional and print on the order [MAN-PUR-72 §11.5].
- The line grid allows only one item per order; create multiple orders for multiple items [MAN-PUR-72 §11.6].
- UOM is read-only [MAN-PUR-72 §11.6].
- Press F2 to search in Supplier code, Source PR (STD only), Tax code, Cost centre, Warehouse, and Item code, or to see rate history in Rate [MAN-PUR-72 §11.4, §11.5, §11.6].
- After entering the supplier and item, press F3 (Fetch) to pull the rate, tax code, payment terms, and warehouse, as well as the cost centre, need-by date, and quantity for STD orders [MAN-PUR-72 §11.3].
- Fetch returns a single-use token (fetch_tok) valid for one supplier and item, which is mandatory to save [MAN-DD-72 §6.8].
- Press F8 to save the order; Bahi validates details, computes tax and gross value (gross = basic + tax), checks the cost centre and budget, and generates the PO number [MAN-DD-72 §6.4, MAN-PUR-72 §11.8].
- The status bar displays `<PO number> SAVED` regardless of the resulting status, so verify the Status field on the header after saving [MAN-PUR-72 §11.8].
- The order saves as Approved (AP) if its gross value is within your limit, or if the source request approver's limit covers the order's gross value [MAN-PUR-72 §11.9].
- If approval limits are not met, the order saves as Pending Approval (PA) and routes to the approver's inbox [MAN-PUR-72 §11.9].
- Saving an order against a request automatically closes (CL) the request [MAN-PUR-72 §11.10].
- Orders can be saved only for ACTIVE suppliers [MAN-PUR-72 §11.11].

## Watch out
- If you change the supplier or item after running Fetch, you must press F3 (Fetch) again; otherwise, saving fails with ERR-SCR-0221 (FETCH NOT DONE) [MAN-PUR-72 §11.3].
- Fetch automatically applies tax code GST18-INTRA; for an out-of-state supplier, manually change this to the appropriate -INTER code before saving or the order fails with ERR-PO-0412 [MAN-PUR-72 §11.4].
- A direct order exceeding the configured company limit (shipped default ₹50,000) fails on save with ERR-PO-0610; raise a purchase request instead [MAN-PUR-72 §11.7].
- Adding a request to a direct order triggers error ERR-PO-0611 [MAN-PUR-72 §11.7].
- Entering a different item or a larger quantity than stated on the source request causes error ERR-PO-0604 [MAN-PUR-72 §11.10].
- Attempting to save an order for a blocked supplier results in error ERR-SUP-0031 [MAN-PUR-72 §11.11].
- If saved against a closed cost centre, the order is set to Draft (DR) with warning W-CC-114 and is not routed to anyone [MAN-DD-72 §6.7, MAN-PUR-72 §11.9].
- Bahi does not verify supplier certificates on the purchase order screen [MAN-PUR-72 §11.11].

# Document Approval Workflows
This page explains how to review, approve, and reject purchase requests and purchase orders in Bahi ERP. Approvers can access pending documents directly from their approval inbox or via email notifications. Completing an approval changes the document status, but approved purchase orders still require release before going to the supplier.

## Rules
- Approvers review purchase requests waiting for them to approve or reject [MAN-PUR-72 §10.1].
- To approve a purchase request, open it from the approval inbox, verify the item, quantity, estimated value, and cost centre, enter a comment, and select Approve to set the status to AP [MAN-PUR-72 §10.2].
- To reject a purchase request, choose Reject and enter a reason to set the status to RJ and notify the raiser by email [MAN-PUR-72 §10.3].
- Approvers view pending orders by navigating to Purchase and then Order approval, where each row lists the document type, number, creator, and creation date [MAN-PUR-72 §12.1].
- Bahi ERP sends an email to the approver whenever a new document arrives in the approval inbox [MAN-PUR-72 §12.1].
- To approve a purchase order, open the document, check its details, and select Approve with an optional comment to change the status to AP [MAN-PUR-72 §12.2].
- To reject a purchase order, press Reject and provide a mandatory reason, which sets the status to RJ and releases the committed budget [MAN-PUR-72 §12.3].
- An approved purchase order with status AP is not sent to the supplier until it is released [MAN-PUR-72 §12.4].

## Watch out
- You cannot approve a purchase request or purchase order that you raised yourself, triggering error ERR-APR-0003 [MAN-PUR-72 §10.2] [MAN-PUR-72 §12.2].
- You cannot approve a purchase request or purchase order with a value exceeding your approval limit, triggering error ERR-APR-0004 [MAN-PUR-72 §10.2] [MAN-PUR-72 §12.2].
- A rejected purchase request cannot be resubmitted; you must create a new request instead [MAN-PUR-72 §10.3].
- You cannot approve a purchase order that is not currently pending approval, which causes error ERR-PO-0702 [MAN-PUR-72 §12.2].

# PO Release, Amendments, and History

This page covers releasing purchase orders to suppliers, changing order details, cancellations, and checking order history. Releasing transmits approved orders to vendors and updates stock tracking. You can also amend active orders, cancel unneeded orders, or review previous purchasing records for an item.

## Rules
- Only purchase orders in status AP can be released to the supplier [MAN-PUR-72 §13.1].
- Open the order and press F9 (Release) to change the status to RL, log the release date, add the quantity to stock on order, and e-mail the order to the supplier's order address [MAN-PUR-72 §13.2].
- The supplier receives the order number, item, quantity, rate, need-by date, delivery warehouse, and any printed remarks [MAN-PUR-72 §13.4].
- You can amend an order's quantity, need-by date, or cost centre, or cancel the order [MAN-PUR-72 §14.1].
- To amend, open the order, update the fields, and press F8; Bahi recalculates the gross value, releases committed budget, checks the new cost centre, and re-commits budget [MAN-PUR-72 §14.2].
- An amended order keeps its current status if the new gross value is still covered by the original approval [MAN-PUR-72 §14.3].
- To fix an order stuck in Draft due to a closed cost centre, amend it to an open cost centre so it can move to AP or PA under normal rules [MAN-PUR-72 §14.4].
- To cancel an order, press Cancel and enter a reason; status changes to CN, committed budget is released, and quantities on released orders are removed from stock on order [MAN-PUR-72 §14.5].
- Purchase order history shows the last ten released orders for an item—optionally filtered by supplier—in newest-first order with quantity, rate, and date [MAN-PUR-72 §15.1].
- Historical rates show previous purchases only; pricing for a new order must come from the current rate contract [MAN-PUR-72 §15.2].
- Search for purchase orders by navigating to Purchase, then Order list, using filters for supplier, item, status, client reference, and creation date [MAN-PUR-72 §15.3].

## Watch out
- Attempting to release an order not in status AP triggers ERR-PO-0715 (DOCUMENT NOT IN RELEASABLE STATUS); status DR usually points to a closed cost centre at save, while PA indicates pending approval [MAN-PUR-72 §13.3].
- Amending an order to a closed cost centre reverts the order to Draft with warning W-CC-114 [MAN-PUR-72 §14.2].
- If an amendment increases the gross value beyond the original approved amount, the order reverts to status PA for re-approval, even if already released [MAN-PUR-72 §14.3].
- Bahi does not notify suppliers of cancellations; you must inform the supplier directly [MAN-PUR-72 §14.5].
- Orders in status CN, RJ, or CL cannot be amended (ERR-PO-0801) [MAN-PUR-72 §14.6].

# Supplier Onboarding and Management

Suppliers must be fully qualified, approved, and active in the ERP system before any purchase order can be placed. This process sets out how purchase executives collect mandatory vendor records, prevent duplicate entries, and manage supplier statuses in Bahi ERP. It applies to all goods and service vendors for the Pune plant and Chakan unit, excluding petty-cash purchases under ₹5,000.

## Rules
- Orders may only be placed with suppliers that hold an ACTIVE status in the supplier master [POL-PUR-001 §6.1].
- New suppliers must be fully onboarded under POL-SUP-003 before placing any purchase order [POL-PUR-001 §6.3].
- The policy covers all suppliers of materials, components, packing, and services to the Pune plant (RSW-PUN-01) and Chakan unit (RSW-CHK-01) [POL-SUP-003 §2.1].
- A purchase executive or senior buyer proposes a new supplier using at least one written quotation and an explanation of why existing suppliers cannot meet the requirement [POL-SUP-003 §3.1].
- Before creating the supplier in Bahi (screen PUR-SUP-01), the proposer must collect the GST registration certificate (GSTIN), PAN, cancelled cheque or bank letter, MSME certificate (if claiming MSME status), and the signed Supplier Code of Conduct [POL-SUP-003 §3.2].
- Proposers must search screen PUR-SUP-03 by name, city, and GSTIN, and attach the search result to the onboarding file [POL-SUP-003 §3.3].
- Always search before creating a supplier; screen PUR-SUP-03 matches any part of the name ignoring case, so search by a short distinctive word and review the entire list [MAN-PUR-72 §5.1, MAN-PUR-72 §5.2].
- The purchase manager must approve the onboarding file before the supplier can be created in Bahi [POL-SUP-003 §3.4].
- Onboarding typically requires five working days from receipt of a complete file [POL-SUP-003 §3.6].
- Supplier master entry (screen PUR-SUP-01) requires Supplier name*, City*, State code* (two letters, e.g., MH, GJ), GSTIN, and Payment terms (F2 lookup; default N30) [MAN-PUR-72 §6.2].
- On Save, Bahi automatically generates the supplier code from the name's initials, the first three letters of the city, and a running sequence number (e.g., DP-RJK-0042) [POL-SUP-003 §5.4, MAN-DD-72 §4.1, MAN-PUR-72 §6.2].
- The master record stores supplier code (`sup_cd`), name, city, state, GSTIN (`gstin`), payment terms (`pt_cd`), status, `created_by`, and `created_on` (migrated suppliers display `MIGRATION`) [MAN-DD-72 §4.1, MAN-DD-72 §4.2, MAN-DD-72 §4.3].
- Double-clicking a supplier in PUR-SUP-03 opens the master view containing GSTIN, address, payment terms, certificates (type, document reference, valid-to date), and rate contracts [MAN-PUR-72 §5.4].
- A supplier is created with ACTIVE status, but no order may be placed until all mandatory onboarding documents—and food-contact certificates where applicable—are on file [POL-SUP-003 §3.5, MAN-PUR-72 §6.4].
- One legal entity must have exactly one active code, and two records with identical GSTINs are treated as the same supplier [POL-SUP-003 §6.1].
- A near-name match in a different city or with a different GSTIN represents a different supplier [POL-SUP-003 §6.3].
- A supplier is BLOCKED if it has been replaced by a new code, failed two consecutive quality audits, or if Finance requests a block due to unpaid debit notes [POL-SUP-003 §5.1].
- Blocked suppliers retain their code and history, display in red in PUR-SUP-03, and cause Bahi to reject new purchase orders with ERR-SUP-0031 [POL-SUP-003 §5.2, MAN-PUR-72 §5.3].
- When a supplier receives a new code, the old code is blocked and renamed "(old code, do not use)" [POL-SUP-003 §5.4, MAN-PUR-72 §5.3].
- Only the purchase manager may request IT in writing to unblock a supplier, stating the reason [POL-SUP-003 §5.3].

## Watch out
- One-time cash purchases under ₹5,000 made via petty-cash imprest do not follow this process and must follow the Finance petty-cash note [POL-SUP-003 §2.2].
- Urgency is never an acceptable reason to skip any onboarding step [POL-SUP-003 §3.6].
- Screen PUR-SUP-03 search does not match spelling variants; for example, searching "Deccan Polymer Industries" will fail to return "Deccan Polymers" [MAN-PUR-72 §5.2].
- Quotations often use shortened vendor names; treat any supplier name close to an existing supplier in the same city as that existing supplier until proven otherwise [POL-SUP-003 §6.2].
- If a duplicate GSTIN is entered on PUR-SUP-01, Save fails with ERR-SUP-0118 [POL-SUP-003 §6.4, MAN-PUR-72 §6.3].
- Bahi cannot catch duplicate suppliers if the GSTIN field is left blank; preventing these duplicates is the proposer's responsibility during the PUR-SUP-03 search [POL-SUP-003 §6.4, MAN-PUR-72 §6.3].
- Bahi will mark a newly saved supplier ACTIVE even if required documents are missing [MAN-PUR-72 §6.4].
- If a duplicate record is created by mistake, report it to the purchase manager the same day, block the duplicate code, and move open documents to the correct code [POL-SUP-003 §6.5].

# Food-Grade Compliance and Certificates
Parts that touch food require a valid food-grade certificate on file before any order is placed. The certificate must be uploaded to the supplier master in Bahi and checked manually by purchasing staff. Expired certificates are invalid and prevent new orders for food-contact parts until renewed.

## Rules
- You may purchase food-contact parts (such as gaskets, lids, body blanks, or any item flagged as food-contact) only from a supplier with a valid food-grade certificate on file in Bahi [POL-PUR-001 §6.2].
- A supplier of any food-contact item must hold a food-grade certificate [POL-SUP-003 §4.1].
- The certificate must be a test report from an accredited food-contact testing laboratory (such as an FSSAI-notified lab) or a BIS conformity certificate for stainless steel grade 304 or higher [POL-SUP-003 §4.2].
- Upload the certificate to the supplier record in Bahi under certificate type `FOOD-GRADE` with its document reference and valid-to date, and have a senior buyer check it before the first order is placed [POL-SUP-003 §4.3].
- To upload in screen PUR-SUP-01, open the supplier, go to the Certificates tab, click Add, enter the Certificate type*, Document reference*, and Valid to* date, attach the scan, and press F8 [MAN-PUR-72 §6.5].
- Bahi records the user who uploaded the certificate and the upload date under `sup_cert` [MAN-DD-72 §4.4, MAN-PUR-72 §6.5].
- A certificate is accepted only if it was issued within the last 24 months and its valid-to date has not expired [POL-SUP-003 §4.4].
- The certificate covers the supplier, but if the supplier changes a material or compound (such as a new silicone grade), it must submit a fresh test report for that specific part [POL-SUP-003 §4.6].
- Quality sets the `food_contact` flag in the item master to 1 if the part touches food, or 0 if it does not [MAN-DD-72 §3.3].

## Watch out
- An expired certificate counts as no certificate; the supplier remains ACTIVE in the master, but you must not order food-contact items until a new certificate is uploaded and verified [POL-PUR-001 §6.2, POL-SUP-003 §4.5].
- Bahi keeps expired certificates on the tab and displays the valid-to date in red, but it does not block purchase orders automatically [POL-SUP-003 §4.7, MAN-PUR-72 §6.6].
- The person raising the purchase order and the order approver must manually verify that the certificate is present and valid [POL-SUP-003 §4.7].

# Rate Contracts and Pricing Policies
Rate contracts set agreed prices for regular items from suppliers over defined validity periods in Bahi ERP. Contracts undergo regular revisions and performance reviews to ensure pricing accuracy and supplier reliability. Orders pull active contract rates automatically to prevent pricing discrepancies.

## Rules
- Prefer suppliers who hold a current rate contract [POL-PUR-001 §6.4].
- Maintain a rate contract in Bahi with a valid-from and valid-to date for each regular supplier of a regular item [POL-SUP-003 §7.1].
- Enter rate contracts on the Rate contracts tab of the supplier master; this task belongs to the purchase manager's office [MAN-PUR-72 §7.1].
- Store contract details using item code, rate, valid-from date, and valid-to date (`sup_rate`: `itm_cd`, `rate`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`) [MAN-DD-72 §4.5].
- Apply a new rate contract starting from its valid-from date, which replaces the previous contract while keeping older rates in history for reference [POL-SUP-003 §7.2].
- Review rate contracts every six months, specifically in March and September [POL-SUP-003 §7.3].
- Review regular suppliers each quarter on delivery on time, rejection rate, and price through the senior buyer [POL-SUP-003 §8.1].
- Press Fetch on the order screen to populate the rate automatically from the contract whose validity period covers the current date [MAN-PUR-72 §7.2].
- Press F2 in the Rate field on the order screen to see all past and present rate contracts for the supplier and item listed from oldest to newest [MAN-PUR-72 §7.3].

## Watch out
- A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not justify switching suppliers for a food-contact part [POL-PUR-001 §6.4].
- If no rate contract covers today's date when you press Fetch, Bahi fills the rate from the last order placed with that supplier for the item and flags the field in yellow [MAN-PUR-72 §7.2].
- A yellow rate field is only a suggestion and must be verified before saving the order [MAN-PUR-72 §7.2].
- Rates from expired contracts or prior purchase orders represent history only and cannot be used as active prices [MAN-PUR-72 §7.3].
- A supplier with a rejection rate above 2% for two consecutive quarters is placed on watch and must be visited by Quality [POL-SUP-003 §8.2].

# Cost Centres and Budget Checks

Every purchase request and order must be assigned to an active cost centre with sufficient funds. Finance manages cost centre statuses and limits, while Bahi ERP tracks committed spend against quarterly budgets. Purchase executives must verify cost centres and budget availability before finalizing orders to prevent processing delays.

## Rules
- Charge every request and order to an open cost centre [POL-PUR-001 §4.1]. Note: POL-PUR-001 §4.1 applies from 2026-04-01 [POL-PUR-001 §4.1].
- Review cost centre details—including code (`cc_cd`), name, status (`OPEN` or `CLOSED`), `closed_on` date, and owner—in Bahi screen `FIN-CC-01` [MAN-DD-72 §9.1] [MAN-PUR-72 §8.1].
- Check the cost centre's status in Bahi screen `FIN-CC-01` or confirm it with Finance before raising an order [POL-PUR-001 §4.3]. Note: POL-PUR-001 §4.3 applies from 2026-04-01 [POL-PUR-001 §4.3].
- Verify available budget, which equals the total period amount minus committed spend (the gross value of approved and pending orders), via the budget check service (`bud_check`) [MAN-DD-72 §9.2] [MAN-DD-72 §9.3] [MAN-PUR-72 §8.4]. For example, the period budget may be set for 2026-Q4 [MAN-DD-72 §9.2].
- Note that Bahi automatically commits an order's gross value against the cost centre once the order is approved [MAN-PUR-72 §8.4].

## Watch out
- Closed cost centres cannot carry new spend; Finance closes them at the end of a production programme [POL-PUR-001 §4.2] [MAN-PUR-72 §8.2].
- If you enter a document against a closed cost centre, Bahi will not reject it outright; it saves it as a Draft, triggers warning `W-CC-114`, and will never send the order to the supplier [POL-PUR-001 §4.2] [MAN-PUR-72 §8.2].
- When you press Fetch, Bahi enters your default cost centre, but IT does not automatically update defaults when Finance closes a cost centre; always check the cost centre before saving [MAN-PUR-72 §8.3].
- If an order's gross value exceeds the available budget, saving the order will fail with error `ERR-BUD-0207` [MAN-PUR-72 §8.4].

# Tax Codes and Payment Terms

This page details the GST tax codes and supplier payment terms used in Bahi ERP. It guides purchase executives on selecting the correct tax codes for intrastate and interstate suppliers. It also defines the standard codes for invoice-based and advance payments.

## Rules

- Effective from 2026-04-01, suppliers in Maharashtra are charged CGST + SGST using tax codes ending in -INTRA, while suppliers in any other state are charged IGST using tax codes ending in -INTER [POL-PUR-001 §8.1].
- Use tax code GST18-INTRA for CGST 9% + SGST 9% when a supplier is in the same state as the organisation unit [MAN-DD-72 §7.1].
- Use tax code GST18-INTER for IGST 18% when a supplier is in another state [MAN-DD-72 §7.2].
- Use tax codes GST12-INTRA and GST12-INTER for the same intrastate and interstate rules at a 12% rate [MAN-DD-72 §7.3].
- Use payment term codes N30, N45, or N60 for net payment at 30, 45, or 60 days from the invoice [MAN-DD-72 §8.1].
- Use payment term code ADV for advance payments [MAN-DD-72 §8.1].

# Items and Inventory Enquiry

Item enquiry (INV-ITM-03) lets you locate item codes, descriptions, and master details before raising purchase requests or orders. Stock enquiry (INV-STK-02) provides real-time warehouse quantities, stock ledgers, and days of cover calculations. Buyers can also view replenishment needs across warehouses using the reorder report.

## Rules

- Use Item enquiry to locate exact item codes in the item master before raising a request or order [MAN-PUR-72 §3.1].
- Find items by entering any part of the description or code in Search text and pressing Enter [MAN-PUR-72 §3.2].
- Search terms ignore case and spaces, and `%` can be used as a wildcard in the middle of a word [MAN-PUR-72 §3.2].
- The search screen displays up to 20 rows; refine your search if the required item does not appear [MAN-PUR-72 §3.2].
- The results list displays the item code, description, unit of measure (UOM), and active status [MAN-PUR-72 §3.3].
- Open the item master view by double-clicking a row or pressing Enter on a selected item [MAN-PUR-72 §3.4].
- The item master view displays the category (RAW, COMPONENTS, SPARES, or PACKING), reorder level, average daily issue, and food-contact flag [MAN-DD-72 §3.4, MAN-PUR-72 §3.4].
- Press F2 inside any Item code field across other screens to open the lookup window, then press Enter to copy the selected code [MAN-PUR-72 §3.5].
- On Stock enquiry (INV-STK-02), the Item code field is mandatory, while the Warehouse field is optional [MAN-PUR-72 §4.2].
- Leave the Warehouse field blank in Stock enquiry to view stock across all warehouses [MAN-PUR-72 §4.2].
- View stock figures directly on screen at the moment you need them because values change throughout the day as stores issue and receive material [MAN-PUR-72 §4.1].
- In the stock enquiry results, "On hand" shows physical stock, "Allocated" shows reservations for production orders, and "On order" shows quantities on released purchase orders not yet received [MAN-PUR-72 §4.3].
- Days of cover is calculated as on-hand stock divided by the item's average daily issue, rounded down [MAN-DD-72 §3.6, MAN-PUR-72 §4.3].
- Click the Ledger button in Stock enquiry to view a read-only list of all receipts and issues for the item, ordered newest first [MAN-PUR-72 §4.4].
- Stock ledger corrections must be made by stores using a stock adjustment requiring stores manager approval [MAN-PUR-72 §4.4].
- Access the reorder list via Reports, then Items below reorder level, to identify items where on-hand plus on-order stock is below the reorder level [MAN-DD-72 §3.6, MAN-PUR-72 §4.5].

## Watch out

- Inactive items (active flag set to 0) appear in grey and cannot be added to new requests or orders [MAN-DD-72 §3.5, MAN-PUR-72 §3.3].
- Do not order item codes ending in `-R` (such as example `GSK-SIL-05L-R`); these are rework items used strictly by Quality [MAN-PUR-72 §3.3].
- The food-contact flag is maintained solely by Quality for parts that contact food during use [MAN-PUR-72 §3.4].
- Do not paste stock figures into emails or documents as permanent numbers because warehouse quantities change constantly [MAN-PUR-72 §4.1].

# Bahi ERP Interface and Navigation

Bahi ERP provides standard screens, keyboard shortcuts, and lookup tools for purchasing tasks. Users log in through the desktop client and can navigate permitted screens, manage documents, and send direct notifications. Always check the status bar for system messages after saving your work.

## Rules
- Start the Bahi client from the desktop icon, enter your user ID and password, and choose your organisation unit [MAN-PUR-72 §2.1].
- Passwords must be at least eight characters, include a digit, and be changed every 90 days via File > Change password [MAN-PUR-72 §2.6].
- Enter codes in capitals or lower case (the system converts lower case to capitals), enter dates as DD-MM-YYYY, and fill all mandatory fields marked with a red asterisk (*) [MAN-PUR-72 §1.3].
- Open screen lookups by pressing F2 or clicking the small F2 button beside a field [MAN-PUR-72 §1.3].
- Press F2 to open lookups for Item code, Supplier code, Cost centre, Warehouse, Tax code, Payment terms, Source PR, and Rate [MAN-PUR-72 §20.1].
- In a lookup window, type to filter the list, navigate with the arrow keys, press Enter to select, or press Esc to exit without changing the field [MAN-PUR-72 §20.2].
- Use the standard function keys to work across screens: F3 to fetch defaults, F5 to refresh from the database, F7 to clear the screen, F8 to save, F9 to submit or release, F10 to access the menu bar, Ctrl+F to find a document by number, and Ctrl+P to print [MAN-PUR-72 §2.5].
- Read the status bar at the bottom after every save; red messages starting with ERR- are errors, and black messages starting with W- are warnings [MAN-PUR-72 §1.3, MAN-PUR-72 §2.3].
- Print documents using Ctrl+P to output to the default printer in your company's layout [MAN-PUR-72 §2.7].
- Click the Notify button on any document to send a logged e-mail or SMS containing the document number to a user or supplier [MAN-PUR-72 §18.2].
- Quote the screen code shown at the right of the title bar (such as PUR-PO-01) whenever you raise a support ticket [MAN-PUR-72 §1.4].

## Watch out
- Entering three wrong passwords locks your user ID for 30 minutes unless IT unlocks it sooner [MAN-PUR-72 §2.1].
- Sessions idle for 20 minutes automatically close; unsaved data is lost because Bahi does not retain half-filled screens across sessions, so save as Draft where available [MAN-PUR-72 §2.4].
- Grey fields are read-only and fill automatically via Fetch or upon saving [MAN-PUR-72 §1.3].
- Screens shown in grey in the navigation tree are installed but not permitted for your user role [MAN-PUR-72 §2.2].
- Bahi does not display pop-up dialogues for most messages, so you must check the status bar directly [MAN-PUR-72 §2.3].
- A purchase order printed before it reaches Released status will show the word DRAFT across the page [MAN-PUR-72 §2.7].
- Saving an order as Draft does not trigger an automated email to anyone [MAN-PUR-72 §18.1].

# Bahi ERP Data Standards and Statuses
This page defines the core data formats, organizational codes, unit of measure standards, and document lifecycle statuses used in Bahi ERP purchasing services. It covers formatting requirements for payloads and explains what each document status means during processing. Use these standards to ensure purchasing records are correctly formatted and tracked.

## Rules
- Service responses return an envelope containing four fields: `rc` (return code: S for success, E for error), `err_cd` (the error code when `rc` is E), `msg` (a short message in capitals), and `data` (the result) [MAN-DD-72 §1.2].
- Dates in payloads must use the format YYYY-MM-DD [MAN-DD-72 §1.3].
- Amounts must be entered in rupees with two decimal places [MAN-DD-72 §1.3].
- System codes must be written in capital letters [MAN-DD-72 §1.3].
- Organisation units use specific codes: RSW-PUN-01 for the Pune plant and RSW-CHK-01 for the Chakan unit, both located in Maharashtra (state code MH) [MAN-DD-72 §2.1].
- Supplier and organisation unit locations use two-letter state codes, such as MH (Maharashtra), GJ (Gujarat), and WB (West Bengal) [MAN-DD-72 §2.2].
- Unit of measure (`uom_cd`) standards are NOS for numbers (pieces) and KG for kilograms [MAN-DD-72 §2.5].
- Supplier status (`status`) must be either ACTIVE or BLOCKED [MAN-DD-72 §2.4].
- Purchasing documents move through seven standard status codes: DR, PA, AP, RL, RJ, CN, and CL [MAN-DD-72 §2.3, MAN-PUR-72 §16.1].
- DR means Draft: the document is saved but not submitted or not valid to proceed, and it is never sent to the supplier [MAN-PUR-72 §16.1].
- PA means Pending approval: the document is waiting in an approver's inbox [MAN-PUR-72 §16.1].
- AP means Approved: the document may now be released [MAN-PUR-72 §16.1].
- RL means Released: the document has been sent to the supplier [MAN-PUR-72 §16.1].
- RJ means Rejected by the approver [MAN-PUR-72 §16.1].
- CN means Cancelled [MAN-PUR-72 §16.1].
- CL means Closed: applies to a request that has been converted into an order [MAN-PUR-72 §16.1].
- Release refers to sending an approved order to the supplier [MAN-PUR-72 §21.1].

## Watch out
- Only orders in RL status have been sent to the supplier; an order in DR, PA, or AP has not reached the supplier [MAN-PUR-72 §16.2].

# System Error Codes and Troubleshooting

Bahi ERP displays error codes and messages to explain why a purchasing transaction cannot proceed. Errors prevent you from saving the document, while warnings allow the record to save. Follow the procedures below to resolve system flags and troubleshoot common purchasing issues.

## Rules
- Read system messages by their code and text; the code indicates which rule failed, the text in brackets shows the failing value, errors stop the Save, and warnings do not [MAN-PUR-72 §17.1].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0412 TAX REGION DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER STATE` by changing the tax code to an `-INTER` code with the same rate (for example, `GST18-INTER`) when the supplier is outside the plant's state, as Fetch always defaults to `GST18-INTRA` [MAN-PUR-72 §17.2].
- Resolve `ERR-SCR-0221 Fetch not done` by pressing F3, reviewing the fetched values, and saving again whenever you change or enter a supplier or item [MAN-PUR-72 §17.3].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0610 Direct PO limit exceeded, raise PR` by raising a purchase request on PUR-PR-01, obtaining approval, and raising a STD order against it [MAN-PUR-72 §17.4].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0611 Direct PO cannot refer PR` by switching the order type to STD or clearing the Source PR field [MAN-PUR-72 §17.5].
- Address warning `W-CC-114 Cost centre closed, document saved as Draft` by amending the order to an open cost centre, noting that the document saves in DR status under `<number> SAVED` while showing the warning on the header and order list [MAN-PUR-72 §17.6].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0602 Source PR mandatory for STD PO` by entering an approved request number, or use a DIR order if the purchase value permits [MAN-PUR-72 §17.7].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0603 Source PR not approved` by following up with the approver or waiting until the request moves to status AP [MAN-PUR-72 §17.8].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0604 Item or quantity not as per PR` by correcting the line details or submitting a new request for the excess quantity [MAN-PUR-72 §17.9].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0201 Quantity must be more than zero` by entering a positive quantity using the item's unit of measure [MAN-PUR-72 §17.10].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0105` and `ERR-PR-0105 Need date in past` by entering today's date or a future date [MAN-PUR-72 §17.11].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0715 Document not in releasable status` by ensuring the purchase order is in AP status before attempting release [MAN-PUR-72 §17.12].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0702 PO not pending approval` by refreshing your inbox to confirm whether another user already acted on the order, as approval actions require PA status [MAN-PUR-72 §17.13].
- Handle `ERR-PO-0801 PO closed` by raising a new order, because orders in CN, RJ, or CL status cannot be amended or cancelled [MAN-PUR-72 §17.14].
- Resolve `ERR-PO-0001 PO not found` by verifying the order number using Ctrl+F or checking the order list [MAN-PUR-72 §17.15].
- Resolve `ERR-SUP-0030 Supplier not found` by pressing F2 in the supplier field or searching in PUR-SUP-03 [MAN-PUR-72 §17.16].
- Resolve `ERR-SUP-0031 Supplier not active` by locating and using the supplier's active replacement code [MAN-PUR-72 §17.17].
- Resolve `ERR-SUP-0118 GSTIN already registered` by searching for and selecting the existing supplier code rather than creating a duplicate record [MAN-PUR-72 §17.18].
- Resolve `ERR-ITM-0010 Item not found` and `ERR-ITM-0011 Item not found or inactive` by using item enquiry to locate an active item code [MAN-PUR-72 §17.19].
- Resolve `ERR-CC-0009 Cost centre not found` by pressing F2 in the Cost centre field to pick a valid code from the list [MAN-PUR-72 §17.20].
- Resolve `ERR-BUD-0207 Budget exceeded` by asking the cost centre owner for an alternative cost centre or requesting a budget transfer from Finance [MAN-PUR-72 §17.21].
- Resolve `ERR-TAX-0101 Invalid tax code` by pressing F2 in the Tax code field to choose an existing code [MAN-PUR-72 §17.22].
- Resolve `ERR-APR-0003 Self approval not allowed` by routing the document to a different authorised approver [MAN-PUR-72 §17.23].
- Resolve `ERR-APR-0004 Value above your limit` by accessing the document from the correct approver's inbox, as Bahi automatically routes orders based on approval limits [MAN-PUR-72 §17.24].
- Resolve `ERR-APR-0009 No approver found` by following company procedures for values exceeding the system's highest approval limit [MAN-PUR-72 §17.25].
- Resolve `ERR-SEC-0001 Not authorised` by requesting role updates through your manager via a written request to IT [MAN-PUR-72 §17.26].
- Resolve `ERR-PR-0007` and `ERR-PR-0008 Request not in the right status` by refreshing the screen and checking the status; ERR-PR-0007 indicates a submitted request was not in Draft, and ERR-PR-0008 indicates approval was attempted on a request not pending approval [MAN-PUR-72 §17.28].
- Troubleshoot orders not received by the supplier by checking status via Ctrl+F; orders in DR may have a closed cost centre, orders in PA await approval, orders in AP must be released, and only RL orders reach the supplier [MAN-PUR-72 §19.1].
- Troubleshoot changed purchase rates by checking current rate contracts via Fetch, as active contract rates replace historical order pricing [MAN-PUR-72 §19.2].
- Troubleshoot missing supplier names by searching for a single short word of the name, verifying the city, and comparing GSTIN records [MAN-PUR-72 §19.3].
- Troubleshoot screen freezes after clicking Save by waiting one minute and searching the order list by supplier, item, date, or client reference before taking further action [MAN-PUR-72 §19.4].
- Troubleshoot approvers unable to see documents by confirming the document was submitted to PA status rather than remaining in DR [MAN-PUR-72 §19.5].

## Watch out
- Do not press Save a second time if the screen hangs; wait one minute and search the order list, as pressing Save again creates a duplicate order [MAN-PUR-72 §19.4].
- Three incorrect user ID or password attempts will trigger `ERR-SEC-0002 Invalid credentials` and lock the user ID [MAN-PUR-72 §17.27].
- Approvers cannot view documents routed above their approval limit; the system automatically pushes higher-value documents to the next manager in the line [MAN-PUR-72 §19.5].

# Purchasing Reports and Analytics
Bahi ERP provides reports to track purchasing operations, pending workflows, and supplier metrics. Purchase executives can run operational reports from the system menu to monitor daily activities and verify compliance. All reports reflect live database values at the exact moment they are generated.

## Rules
- Access reports through the Reports menu, enter the required values in the parameter window, and press F8 to run the report [MAN-PUR-72 §22.1].
- Export report grid results to a spreadsheet using Ctrl+E [MAN-PUR-72 §22.1].
- Run the Open Orders by Supplier report to view orders in status AP or RL that are not fully received, grouped by supplier with outstanding quantities and need-by dates [MAN-PUR-72 §22.2].
- Use the Orders Pending Approval report to view all requests and orders in status PA, including the assigned approver and days waiting [MAN-PUR-72 §22.3].
- Run the Draft Orders report to see every order in status DR alongside its warning code [MAN-PUR-72 §22.4].
- Use the Price Variance report to compare released order rates against active rate contracts within an entered tolerance [MAN-PUR-72 §22.5].
- Track expiring supplier documents by running the Certificate Expiry report for a specified number of days and certificate type [MAN-PUR-72 §22.6].
- Review cost centre budgets, committed amounts, and available balances for a quarter using the Budget Utilisation report [MAN-PUR-72 §22.7].
- Generate the Supplier Performance report to view released orders, on-time deliveries, and rejections for a chosen period [MAN-PUR-72 §22.8].

## Watch out
- Run the Draft Orders report every morning; orders in status DR have not been sent to the supplier, and the system notifies no one when an order is saved as Draft [MAN-PUR-72 §22.4].
- Finance owns the figures shown in the Budget Utilisation report, which simply reads the values present when generated [MAN-PUR-72 §22.7].
- Rejection data in the Supplier Performance report relies on Quality entering rejections on the goods-inspection screen [MAN-PUR-72 §22.8].

# System Administration and Version Migration

This page outlines key administrative functions, user settings, and audit rules in Bahi ERP 7.2. It also explains core system changes and data behavior when migrating from Bahi 6.x. IT manages user roles and parameters, while specific approval limits attach directly to individual user accounts.

## Rules
- IT creates users on the security console and assigns each user one role [MAN-PUR-72 §23.1].
- A user's role controls which screens appear in the navigation tree and which services the user can call [MAN-PUR-72 §23.1].
- Approval limits are stored on the user record rather than the role, following the company approval matrix [MAN-PUR-72 §23.1].
- Integrations connect via service accounts, which are treated like regular users with their own roles, approval limits, and document creation records [MAN-PUR-72 §23.2].
- Companies should restrict service accounts to only the specific services they need [MAN-PUR-72 §23.2].
- IT sets a user's default cost centre on the user record, which is used by Fetch [MAN-PUR-72 §23.3].
- The direct-order limit is a company-wide setting maintained by IT on the purchasing parameters screen [MAN-PUR-72 §23.4].
- Updates to the direct-order limit take effect the next time each user signs in [MAN-PUR-72 §23.4].
- Every service call logs the time, user, service, payload, return code, and error code to the audit trail [MAN-PUR-72 §23.5].
- The audit trail cannot be edited from any screen [MAN-PUR-72 §23.5].
- Bahi 7 splits the single Bahi 6.x order screen into separate entry, approval, and release screens, adds the Fetch requirement, and moves approval limits from roles to users [MAN-PUR-72 §24.1].
- Supplier codes migrated from 6.x retain their old format and show MIGRATION as the creator [MAN-PUR-72 §24.1].
- Orders migrated from 6.x appear only with status RL or CL [MAN-PUR-72 §24.2].
- Migrated orders keep their original rates and tax codes from 6.x without recalculation [MAN-PUR-72 §24.2].

## Watch out
- Default cost centres are not updated automatically by Bahi when Finance closes cost centres; administrators must review and update user records manually [MAN-PUR-72 §23.3].

# Salary Bands 2026-27 (Confidential)
This page sets the confidential pay bands and rules for the purchase department for 2026-27. It outlines fixed pay ranges, variable pay targets, and increment limits. These rules take effect on 2026-04-01.

## Rules
- Annual fixed pay for a purchase executive (PUR-EXEC, Band M2) ranges from ₹6,40,000 to ₹8,90,000 [HR-CONF-007 §2.1].
- Annual fixed pay for a senior buyer (PUR-SR, Band M3) ranges from ₹9,20,000 to ₹12,60,000 [HR-CONF-007 §2.1].
- Annual fixed pay for a purchase manager (PUR-MGR, Band M4) ranges from ₹14,50,000 to ₹19,80,000 [HR-CONF-007 §2.1].
- Annual fixed pay for a plant head (PLANT-HEAD, Band L1) ranges from ₹38,00,000 to ₹52,00,000 [HR-CONF-007 §2.1].
- Variable pay reaches up to 12% of fixed pay, paid in May based on annual savings against rate contracts [HR-CONF-007 §2.2].
- The 2026-27 increment pool is set at 9.5% of fixed pay [HR-CONF-007 §3.1].
- All rules apply starting 2026-04-01 [HR-CONF-007 §1.1].

## Watch out
- Do not share this page with employees, managers outside HR, or any system serving other staff [HR-CONF-007 §1.1].
- Any individual increment above 14% requires approval from the plant head [HR-CONF-007 §3.1].

# Food-Grade Compliance and Certificates

Parts that touch food may only be purchased from suppliers with an approved, valid food-grade certificate on file in Bahi ERP. Buyers must verify the certificate before placing an order because the system does not automatically block non-compliant purchases. Quality sets the food-contact flag on items, and certificates must be kept up to date to prevent supply disruptions.

## Rules
- Food-contact parts (such as gaskets, lids, body blanks, or any item flagged as food-contact in the item master) can only be purchased from a supplier holding a valid food-grade certificate uploaded in Bahi [POL-PUR-001 §6.2].
- Quality sets the `food_contact` flag to 1 in the item master if the part touches food in use [MAN-DD-72 §3.3].
- A supplier of any food-contact item must hold a food-grade certificate [POL-SUP-003 §4.1].
- The certificate must be an accredited laboratory test report for food-contact materials (such as an FSSAI-notified lab) or a BIS conformity certificate for stainless steel grade 304 or higher [POL-SUP-003 §4.2].
- Certificates are uploaded against the supplier under certificate type `FOOD-GRADE` with document reference and valid-to date, and must be checked by the senior buyer before the first order [POL-SUP-003 §4.3].
- Upload certificates in Bahi screen PUR-SUP-01 by going to the supplier's Certificates tab, clicking Add, entering Certificate type, Document reference, Valid to date, attaching the scanned file, and pressing F8 until "CERT SAVED" appears [MAN-PUR-72 §6.5].
- Bahi records the user who uploaded the certificate and the upload date under `uploaded_by` and `uploaded_on` [MAN-DD-72 §4.4, MAN-PUR-72 §6.5].
- Currently, a certificate is accepted if issued within the last 24 months and not expired; effective 1 September 2026, it is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the order date [POL-SUP-003 §4.4, AMD-SUP-2026-02 §1.1].
- Before raising an order for a food-contact part, staff must verify the certificate's issue date and valid-to date against the active rule [AMD-SUP-2026-02 §3.1].
- If a supplier changes the material or compound of a part (such as a new silicone grade), they must submit a fresh test report for that specific part [POL-SUP-003 §4.6].
- On the first working day of every month, the senior buyer must run the certificate-expiry report with a 90-day window and contact every supplier whose food-grade certificate expires within that period [AMD-SUP-2026-02 §3.2].

## Watch out
- Bahi does not automatically stop or block orders to suppliers lacking a certificate or holding an expired certificate; the person raising the order and the approver must manually check compliance [POL-SUP-003 §4.7, MAN-PUR-72 §6.6].
- An expired certificate counts as no certificate; the supplier remains ACTIVE in the master, but no food-contact parts may be ordered until a new certificate is uploaded and verified [POL-PUR-001 §6.2, POL-SUP-003 §4.5].
- Bahi retains expired certificates on the tab for record-keeping and highlights passed valid-to dates in red [MAN-PUR-72 §6.6].
- From 1 September 2026, any certificate meeting the old rule (issued within 24 months and not expired) but failing the new rule counts as no certificate for new orders, though orders released before that date remain valid [AMD-SUP-2026-02 §1.2].

# Purchase Order Entry and Rules

The purchase order entry screen creates standard and direct orders to suppliers. Standard orders require an approved purchase request, while direct orders cover low-value purchases without a request. Every order requires running the Fetch action before saving and must pass system validations.

## Rules
- Standard (STD) purchase orders must be raised against an approved purchase request entered in the Source PR field [MAN-PUR-72 §11.2].
- A direct (DIR) order has no request, must not refer to a request, and is permitted only up to a gross value (including GST) of ₹50,000; note that starting 2026-12-01, this limit is reduced to ₹25,000 [POL-PUR-001 §3.3, AMD-PUR-2026-03 §1.1, AMD-PUR-2026-03 §1.2, MAN-PUR-72 §11.2, MAN-PUR-72 §11.7].
- A purchase order raised against a request cannot exceed the requested quantity or differ in item from the request [POL-PUR-001 §3.4, MAN-PUR-72 §11.10].
- Bahi ERP assigns order numbers using the format PO/<year>/<five digits>, such as PO/2026/01182 [MAN-DD-72 §6.1, MAN-PUR-72 §11.8].
- Mandatory header fields include Supplier code, Order type (STD or DIR), Tax code, Cost centre, and Need-by date; Source PR is mandatory for STD orders [MAN-DD-72 §6.2, MAN-PUR-72 §11.5].
- Mandatory line fields are Item code, Quantity, and Rate [MAN-PUR-72 §11.6].
- Line unit of measure (UOM) is read-only, and each order supports only one item line [MAN-PUR-72 §11.6].
- After entering the supplier and item, you must press F3 (Fetch) to retrieve the rate, tax code, payment terms, and warehouse, as well as cost centre, need-by date, and quantity for STD orders [MAN-PUR-72 §11.3].
- Fetch generates a one-time token valid for one supplier and item; you must run Fetch again if you alter either field [MAN-DD-72 §6.8, MAN-PUR-72 §11.3].
- To save, press F8; the system validates details, calculates tax and gross value (gross = basic + tax), verifies cost centres and budgets, and generates the PO number [MAN-DD-72 §6.4, MAN-PUR-72 §11.8].
- Saving an order against a purchase request automatically marks that request closed (CL) [MAN-PUR-72 §11.10].
- If an order's gross value falls within your limit, or if the source request approver's limit covers the order's gross value, the order saves with status AP (approved); otherwise, it saves as PA (pending approval) and routes to the approver's inbox [MAN-PUR-72 §11.9].
- Purchase orders can only be saved for suppliers with ACTIVE status [MAN-PUR-72 §11.11].

## Watch out
- Trying to save without running Fetch for the current supplier and item fails with error ERR-SCR-0221 (FETCH NOT DONE) [MAN-PUR-72 §11.3].
- Fetch defaults the tax code to GST18-INTRA; for an out-of-state supplier, you must manually change this to the appropriate -INTER code before saving, or the save fails with ERR-PO-0412 [MAN-PUR-72 §11.4].
- Entering a request on a DIR order causes error ERR-PO-0611 [MAN-PUR-72 §11.7].
- A direct order exceeding the allowable gross limit fails with ERR-PO-0610 (currently above ₹50,000; applies above ₹25,000 starting 2026-12-01) [MAN-PUR-72 §11.7, AMD-PUR-2026-03 §3.1].
- Entering a quantity greater than the request or choosing a different item triggers ERR-PO-0604 [MAN-PUR-72 §11.10].
- Attempting to save an order with a blocked supplier triggers ERR-SUP-0031 [MAN-PUR-72 §11.11].
- If an order is saved against a closed cost centre, it saves as DR (Draft) with warning W-CC-114 and will not be routed to anyone; always check the Status field on the header after saving [MAN-DD-72 §6.7, MAN-PUR-72 §11.8, MAN-PUR-72 §11.9].
